dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing sudden vertigo; could you describe the sensation and tell me exactly when it began? (Question 1/20)

It felt like the entire room was suddenly spinning around me while I was trying to get into bed last night. It was very intense and made me quite sick to my stomach, but the whole thing only lasted about three minutes.
That sounds very distressing. Have you noticed any changes in your hearing, such as ringing in your ears or a feeling of fullness? (Question 2/20)
No, my hearing seems completely normal and I haven't noticed any ringing or fullness in my ears. I also haven't had any headaches or trouble moving my arms or legs.

Does this spinning sensation happen specifically when you roll over in bed or tilt your head back to look up at something? Also, I'd like to perform a physical exam to check for specific eye movements. (Question 3/20)

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike_Maneuver
RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.
Thank you for participating in that test. Have you ever experienced these dizzy spells before, or was last night the first time? (Question 4/20)
No, doctor, I've never felt anything like this in my life before. I'm generally a healthy person, aside from some eczema, so this whole experience has been quite a shock.

I appreciate you sharing that information with me. Based on your description of the spinning and the positive result from the Dix-Hallpike maneuver, I have reached a conclusion.

DIAGNOSIS READY
